I am old now, 72 years, and I plant my cassava the way my mother taught me. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer from the shop, and for cassava we do not need it — the roots grow well in our soil here in Kigoma. I keep the cuttings from last season's harvest, the local kind that does well even when the rains are short. Because my back is not strong, I will pay one of my neighbour's sons for a few days to help me clear and mound the soil.
